solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very small boy, this person's Irish or Russian?

parts.note: a lad is a young boy
the setter speaking of himself: this person is = I am, contracted to I'M

explanation.surface: A question about whether a tiny lad, perhaps the speaker himself, is Irish or Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person's' reads as a possessive but is 'this person is', the setter's I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male forename in Russia, borne by Lenin and Putin, so it stands for a Russian by example.

clue.text: Carriage light has glow reduced by half

parts.note: to light on something is to come down on it, to land

indicators.note: the word for glow loses half of its four letters, keeping only the front pair

parts.note: an aura is a glow surrounding something

explanation.surface: A lamp whose glow has been dimmed by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a noun (a lamp) but is the verb meaning to settle or come down; AURA halved gives AU.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood, a type of carriage.

clue.text: Plan to have day with crowd

parts.note: a raft of things is a large number or crowd of them

explanation.surface: Arranging to spend a day amid a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, a synonym for a plan.

clue.text: First person leading everyone within distance must surely be this!

definitions.text: First person leading everyone within distance must surely be this!

indicators.note: one piece goes in front of the rest of the wordplay, at the head

parts.note: the first-person pronoun in its object form is me

indicators.note: the word for everyone sits inside the abbreviation for distance

parts.note: DIST is a standard abbreviation for distance
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Whoever finishes first, ahead of the whole field over the course, surely wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of a race winner, who leads everyone over the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who leads the whole field across the course finishes first and is awarded a gold, making them a prizewinner.

clue.text: Diamond maybe that a footballer doesn't want

definitions.meaning: a diamond in a pack of playing cards is a red suit
a referee shows a player this to send him off the pitch

explanation.surface: A precious stone that no footballer would wish for, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds and hearts are red playing cards; in football, the referee's dismissal card is red.

clue.text: Nasty type, head of colony is held to be unfair to indigenous people?

indicators.note: the rodent word keeps the next letters held inside it

parts.note: a rat is a nasty, treacherous person

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of colony

explanation.surface: An unpleasant colonial governor is accused of mistreating the natives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty type' looks like the definition, but it supplies the outer piece; the definition is the final phrase, marked by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating native peoples unfairly on grounds of their ethnicity is prejudice of the bigoted kind.

clue.text: Setter-up of a site of civilisation

definitions.text: Setter-up of a site of civilisation

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Sumer, in ancient Mesopotamia, is regarded as one of the earliest civilisations

explanation.surface: Who founded a cradle of civilisation?
explanation.walkthrough: With 'up' as a reversal in a down clue, SUMER turned gives the founder of Rome, itself a site of civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Romulus and his twin brother founded the city of Rome, so the twin is a founder of that civilisation.

clue.text: Elliott, for example, being involved in act with E.T. once

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: the letters of the film alien's name

explanation.surface: The boy from the film E.T. once had a part in a scene with the alien.
explanation.walkthrough: Elliott is the boy in Spielberg's E.T. whom the alien reaches; 'being involved' mixes ACT, ET and ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elliott is the human the extraterrestrial makes contact with, so he is an example of someone contacted.

clue.text: People pretending to be saints receiving censure

indicators.note: the two saint letters take in the word for censure between them

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for saint, doubled for plural saints
to hammer someone is to criticise them severely

explanation.surface: Impostors posing as saints are being condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: To sham is to fake or feign, so those who sham are pretenders.

clue.text: Many a nurse will be advancing

definitions.meaning: nurses are often working in a hospital ward, i.e. on the ward

explanation.surface: Plenty of nurses will be getting promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, ON WARD, for where a nurse works.
explanation.definitionFit: Onward is moving forwards or further ahead, which is what advancing means.

clue.text: Protest against return of murderer who is devilishly wicked?

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: the murderer's name is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer

explanation.surface: A protest against a killer's release, calling him fiendish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' suggests a murderer coming back; it reverses CAIN to NIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoniac means possessed by a demon or fiendish, so it describes someone devilishly evil.

clue.text: Guy goes to work with a cloak

parts.note: a guy is a man
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A man heads off to his job wearing a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace or silk scarf or light cape worn over the head and shoulders, a short cloak.

clue.text: Instruments in script by playwright

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a written script

explanation.surface: Musical instruments mentioned in a dramatist's text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside: the manuscript abbreviation sits next to the dramatist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shawms are medieval double-reed woodwind instruments, forerunners of the oboe.

clue.text: By implication resists women with fateful influence?

parts.note: the word resists is what you get from a weird (oddly arranged) version of the word sisters

explanation.surface: Someone opposes powerful women only indirectly.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'weird' signals jumbled, so a jumbled SISTERS yields 'resists', which the clue shows.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth the three witches who foretell his fate are named by this phrase, sisters of destiny.

clue.text: Getting into battle with something to kill rats? Good!

parts.note: warfarin is an anticoagulant used as a rat poison

explanation.surface: Waging war on rodents with poison, and doing well at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfaring is engaging in war, so it describes going into combat.

clue.text: Offended when article's penned that shouldn't be giving anyone a shock?

definitions.text: that shouldn't be giving anyone a shock?

indicators.note: the article is shut inside, as in a pen, within the word for offended

parts.note: insulted means offended
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence at a newspaper piece that ought not to shock its readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests outrage, but the definition is electrical: wiring that is covered cannot jolt you.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiring wrapped in non-conducting material cannot deliver an electric jolt to whoever touches it.

clue.text: Navigation of boat at sea entering enclosure

indicators.note: the jumbled boat letters go into the enclosure word

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of boat are muddled

explanation.surface: A boat making its way through the water into a harbour pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabotage is coastal trade and sailing between ports, a form of seafaring along a country's shores.

clue.text: Fish appearing in various ports was rare

indicators.note: various means of different kinds, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish seen in several harbours used to be uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: Parrotfish and the related parrot-wrasse are colourful reef fish with beak-like mouths.

clue.text: Epistle by St Paul with hard language

parts.note: Romans is Paul's letter to the church in Rome
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A letter from the apostle written in a difficult tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Romansh is a Romance tongue spoken in parts of Switzerland, one of its national languages.

clue.text: How Cockney may comment on high temperature creates a problem for the listener!

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: a remark on the heat: 'hot, it is'

explanation.surface: A Londoner remarking on the heat causes trouble for anyone listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listener' looks like an audience member but means the ear: the comment 'Hot, it is' loses its opening H in Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Otitis is inflammation of the ear, an ailment that affects your hearing organ.

clue.text: Little lake, only 'half a lake' in that country

indicators.note: the half-lake letters go inside the word for little lake

parts.note: a pond is a small lake

indicators.note: takes the front two of the four letters of lake

explanation.surface: A country described by its small lakes, each only half a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Poland is a central European nation, so it is an instance of a country.

clue.text: Stop being sweet

definitions.meaning: an organ stop with a soft, sweet tone bears this Italian name
Italian for sweet, used as a musical direction meaning softly and sweetly

explanation.surface: Quit being nice.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical term for softly, also the name of a gentle organ stop.

clue.text: Chap leading silent dog

indicators.note: the word for chap goes in front of the word for silent

parts.note: a chap is a male
mute means silent

explanation.surface: A man walking ahead of a quiet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The malemute is a large Arctic sled dog, an Alaskan breed related to the husky.

clue.text: Take a little time with container of ashes maybe — to do this?

definitions.text: Take a little time with container of ashes maybe — to do this?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
an urn often holds a person's cremated remains

explanation.surface: Spend a while beside the funeral urn, and grieve?
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue pictures someone pausing by a loved one's urn, which is the act of grieving.
explanation.definitionFit: Pausing by a container of someone's ashes is what grieving people do, so the clue describes lamenting the dead.

clue.text: Soft food that's bad on the menu? It'll do for the dog

parts.note: pap is soft, mushy food
ill means bad, as in ill will
a dish that is on is available on the menu

explanation.surface: Mushy, nasty food served at a restaurant is only fit for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It'll do for the dog' suggests a scrap fit for a pet; the dog is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The papillon is a small toy spaniel breed named for its butterfly-shaped ears.

clue.text: Reliable but not totally up to scratch after short time

indicators.note: the out-of-practice word comes after the abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
rusty means out of practice, not quite up to standard

explanation.surface: Dependable, though a bit out of practice after a brief break.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty means faithful and dependable, a synonym for something you can rely on.

clue.text: Fever in filthy place with half the visitors wiped out

parts.note: a den is a squalid room or haunt

indicators.note: only the front half of the visitors word survives
the rest of the visitors word is removed, leaving its first half

parts.note: guests are visitors

explanation.surface: An illness strikes a squalid lodging, killing half the guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Dengue is a tropical viral illness spread by mosquitoes, known as breakbone fever.

clue.text: Fellow into crime may be one with the wrong idea about good life?

definitions.text: one with the wrong idea about good life?

indicators.note: the word for fellow goes inside the word for crime

parts.note: a heist is a robbery, a crime
a don is a college fellow at a university

explanation.surface: A man drawn into lawlessness may have mistaken notions of how to live well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' suggests HE or MAN, but it is a university DON. The question mark flags the setter's own view that pleasure-seeking is the wrong idea of the good life.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist holds that pleasure is the highest good, a view the setter teasingly calls mistaken.
